content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I am trying to monitor a [product_name] module either via an Android app, a web server, or AWS IoT. From what I understand, I need to configure a modem with the device's IP address (Case 1). For the Android app option: After completing the modem setup, do I need to connect my phone to the same modem as the device to access it, or can I connect from any location via the internet? Is it possible to access remotely without requiring internet service from a provider? For the web server: Do I need internet service from a provider for the modem connected to the device? Again, is remote access possible, or is it limited to the factory location? For AWS IoT: Can I connect to the [product_name] module in RUN mode from anywhere, provided the modem has internet access from a provider?

Hi, If you wish to connect to any device over the internet, you will need an internet provider regardless. If you already have internet access, just connect your [product_name] to your network. Typically, you can set up your internet router so that a VPN allows you to securely connect to your network and the [product_name]. If no internet is available, a 4G/LTE router with a SIM card and internet access is needed; ideally, the SIM should have a public IP address. Running an app, web server, and cloud connection simultaneously on one [product_name] module is not possible, as it doesn't support both web server and cloud communication at the same time. If you just need access from one device, the internal web server may be best. You can create a custom web page using the [product_name] web editor tool. This user-created web page can be opened using any internet browser, whether on smartphone, tablet, PC, or TV. There are plenty of tutorial videos available on YouTube. Hope this helps.
For accessing the web server, do I need to be physically at the factory near the [product_name] and its modem, or is remote access possible from a distant location, such as from home?

Hi, If your [product_name] module with the web server enabled is connected to your local network and you can access your network remotely via VPN, remote access will work. Here’s a suggested approach: 1. Set up and configure the web server on your [product_name] module. 2. Connect the module to your local network; if WiFi is available, use a smartphone, tablet, or PC and verify access via a browser. 3. Configure your internet router for VPN-based remote access to your local network. 4. Test remote connectivity to the web server on your [product_name] module through the internet using a remote device. Hope this helps.

Hello! For remote access, you could install a compatible device at the factory and connect your [product_name] module to it. For example, see [url]. Once set up, you can configure remote access from your home computer.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring ways to monitor and control a [product_name] module remotely, using options like a mobile app, web server, and AWS IoT. There is uncertainty about network requirements, especially concerning remote access outside the local environment. Users have discovered that simultaneous cloud and web server operation isn't supported by a single device, and remote accessibility depends on VPN setup or proper network configuration. There haven't been any reports of device or software errors, but some users feel limited by the device's inability to handle integrated remote access.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward remote access and monitoring of their [product_name] module from any location via smartphone, web browser, or cloud connection. Ideally, this would require minimal network setup and few external requirements.
